english.title: Racially / religiously aggravated stalking involving fear of violence
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) pursued a course of conduct, namely **(..SPECIFY THE COURSE OF CONDUCT..), which amounted to stalking causing **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) to fear, on at least two occasions, that violence would be used against

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

when you knew or ought to have known that your course of conduct would cause that person fear of violence on each occasion and the offence was

(C)_[racially]_
(D)_[religiously]_

aggravated within the terms of section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998
english.legislation: Contrary to section 32(1)(b) and (4) of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 and section 4A(1)(b)(i) of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997.

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)

english.notes:
(i) For the non-racially / religiously aggravated version of this offence, see document H18817.
(ii) For racially / religiously aggravated stalking involving serious alarm or distress, see document H22542.
(iii) Where both, racial and religious hostility, are involved two offences should be charged.
(iv) The option to return an alternative verdict of guilty of the basic offence is not available in the magistrates' court, therefore the basic offence should be charged in addition to the aggravated offence. If on trial on indictment, the jury find the suspect not guilty of the offence charged, they may find him guilty of the basic offence in section 4A of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997; it is good practice to charge both.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 14 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
